title: Question template
description: The machine twin of one catalog entry in questions.md 2 — one file per entry under eval/templates/. It carries what generation needs (parameters, pools, validity requirements) and what scoring needs (the A:/Traj:/Must-not:/Cards: fields and the tolerance). The scoring fields are COPIED into every case at generation, never referenced across files, so a scorer reads one record and never opens a second (agent_architecture.md 6.1). The tool and card vocabularies live once, in case.schema.json, and are referenced from here. One constraint is deliberately not expressed below: a gold tool may not also appear in must_not_tools, which compares two sibling arrays and so belongs to the generator's own assertions rather than to a schema.

id.description: The catalog id, e.g. T09 or T16a. One template file per entry, a/b variants included.

category.description: The catalog's family letter: A pure SQL, B pure lookup, C pure weather, D model chains, E hybrid, F given-values controls, G counterfactuals, H presentation, I modelling availability.

split.description: `train+seen` is carried by train and test_seen alike; `unseen` is holdout, and is the b-side of a train-side pair moving exactly one named axis.

documentary_reference.description: Whether the question names the documentation, or asks what a documented value is. This is questions.md 1.6's route cue, and it is machine-checkable on purpose: paraphrase generation may neither add nor remove such a reference, and a template whose flag disagrees with its gold set is the T07 / T16a / T16b defect returning.

params.description: One entry per `{placeholder}` the question sketch carries. Sampled values are written into the case's inputs.params, and the per-param disjointness constraint is enforced in generation over these keys.

roof_pool.description: questions.md 1.8's pools. P1 the full roster, P1f its flux-instrumented subset, P2 the substrate roofs both water balances cover, `non_modellable` the two roofs family I samples from outside the pools. Absent where the template names no roof.

kind.description: `not_available` is an abstention case, whose contract status is not_available and whose answer is null. `artifact` is family H's plot deliverable: status answered, answer null. Both project to answer_metric `skipped`.

balanced.description: Rejection-sample until the two classes are ~50/50 within each split. Meaningful for `bool` only, and it is why train's m is an even 4.

expected_tool_calls.description: The gold trajectory, copied into every case. An empty array is meaningful: T18b's abstention has no tool signal at all.

alternative_expected_tool_calls.description: Additional gold trajectories, any one of which satisfies the template. Used only where two routes return the identical number and the docstring recommends either (T25).

argument_checks.description: As in a case, except that a `value` may carry `{param}` placeholders, substituted at generation from the sampled parameters.

oracle.description: The function that materializes the answer. It imports the tool chain's own code, so oracle and tool cannot diverge.

data_requirements.description: The (table, column, window) set questions.md 1.6's three validity predicates are evaluated over — through the as-of view, and anchored at seed_at for seed-bearing families.

notes.description: The catalog's Note: field — why the template exists. Prose, not read by any scorer.

surface.description: One language's question surface. `sketch` carries `{param}` placeholders and is what P7's paraphrase generation rewrites; `examples` are hand-written illustrations, not a pool.

pool.description: An explicit value pool. Mutually exclusive with `source`.

source.description: A named derivation the generator resolves against the pinned record — e.g. `rain_events` (scripts/count_t12_rain_events.py's qualifying set), `as_of_band`, `roof_pool`. Mutually exclusive with `pool`.

disjoint_between_splits.description: train ∩ test_seen = ∅ on this parameter's sampled values. True by default and false only where the axis is deliberately shared, as roof is.

column.description: A column name, or the literal `{roof}` meaning that roof's column in this table, read off roofs.py — which is where a roof's absence from a table is recorded, and is why P1f exists.

state_column.description: Whether the frozenness predicate applies. A flux resting at zero is reporting the truth, so the run test is for state columns only, and never for the gravel roof's.

kind.description: `point` needs its day at 44 of 48 rows; `period` needs 95 % of expected rows with no gap over 24 h.

anchor.description: What the window is measured from: the case's `as_of`, the seed rule's `seed_at = min(window_start, as_of)`, or a sampled parameter named `param:<name>`.
